short_desc: Numeric values you can do arithmetic on.
detail: The reader-level number family. Format = <symbols>[range].precision: symbols to strip/expect, an interval domain, and decimal precision.

short_desc: A measured or counted magnitude (default number class).
detail: The least-restrictive number class: a plain magnitude.
A non-negative whole tally. Interval [0,Inf) with .0 precision (integer).

short_desc: A measured value on a unit scale.
detail: A continuous measurement; unit kept in dd_data_unit.

validation: denominator & period declared ;; nonnegative where applicable
short_desc: An amount per unit of exposure or time.
detail: A quantity normalized by a denominator or period.
Numerator over denominator; denominator nonzero.

short_desc: A constructed index relative to a base.
detail: A composite indicator with a documented base period.

validation: allowed range ;; permitted increments ;; scale direction
short_desc: A score on a defined scale.
detail: Points on an instrument or test.

validation: positive integer ;; bounded by group size
detail: Integer position within an ordering.

short_desc: An elapsed amount of time as a number.
detail: A length of time as a numeric magnitude; unit in dd_data_unit.

validation: numeric after symbol/grouping strip ;; decimal precision
detail: Money. as_currency strips symbol/grouping to a number; currency label in dd_data_unit; stable_data_format records usd (kept) vs plain (stripped).
A monetary balance that may be negative.

short_desc: A part of a whole, bounded.
detail: A share bounded to a range; subclasses fix the bounds.
A proportion on a 0-100 scale; as_percent strips a trailing %.
A likelihood bounded to the unit interval.
Rank against a reference population on 0-100.

short_desc: A low-high numeric pair in one field.
detail: Two numeric bounds in one cell; format shows the join (lo-hi, lo to hi).
A low-high interval around an estimate, with a confidence level.
A single-axis map coordinate in a declared CRS. A packed lat/lon pair is structured.geometry. CRS in dd_data_unit.
Decimal-degree latitude (WGS84 by default).
Decimal-degree longitude (WGS84 by default).
The reader-level text family. Classes refine the semantic kind of string.
Unstructured string with no finer role.
A brief descriptive label (not a controlled category).
A work or section title.

validation: preserve line breaks ;; flag control characters
detail: Multi-sentence notes or descriptions.

validation: valid syntax (promote to structured if parsed)
detail: Structured data carried as a string.

validation: trim ;; normalize repeated spaces ;; flag digits/invalid punctuation
detail: A person, organization, place, or account name.
An individual's name; format notes the ordering convention.
A legal or organization name.
A named place as free text (a geographic code is categorical.geographic).

validation: platform charset & length ;; unique where a key
detail: An account handle on a platform. Name-like as an attribute; promote to identifier when it keys the account. Platform in the format namespace (handle:twitter); the @ is auto-stripped/restored.

validation: min component presence ;; postal-code consistency ;; normalize street suffixes
detail: A mailing address of a physical place. The physical counterpart to text.web (virtual addresses).
The street line of an address.
A post-office box address.
A complete one-line or multi-part mailing address.
An address that locates a digital resource (URL, domain, IP, MAC). The digital parallel to a physical postal address.

validation: valid URI syntax ;; allowed schemes ;; add scheme if missing
detail: A web address; as_url canonicalizes (adds scheme, lowercases host, normalizes www, drops trailing slash).
A bare host name without scheme or path.
An IPv4 or IPv6 network address.
A hardware MAC address.

short_desc: A channel to reach a person.
detail: A way to contact someone (email, phone). Email straddles web and contact; kept here by role.

validation: email pattern ;; lowercase domain ;; optional uniqueness
detail: An RFC-style email address.
A telephone number; no single canonical form (user chooses stable representation).

validation: valid color syntax ;; channel range check
detail: A color in some model; the model is carried in data_format, not a subclass.

validation: allowed-values list ;; unexpected-level check ;; missing codes separated
short_desc: A value from a discrete set of levels.
detail: The categorical family. Format = the encoding shape (code / label / code=label); the level dictionary lives in dd_f_levels.

validation: exactly one level per record ;; reference level declared
short_desc: Exactly one level per record (default categorical class).
detail: A standard single-select category.
Levels with no meaningful order.
Order carried by the order field in dd_f_levels.

validation: reference-list lookup ;; level declared ;; hierarchy consistency
detail: A geography used as a grouping variable. Format defers to the geographic tokens (fips:*, metro:*, usps:*). Promoted to identifier.id.geographic when near-unique.
A code from a standard classification. Format = class:<system> (naics, icd10, icd9, soc).

validation: mutually exclusive ;; separate from substantive values
detail: Categories explaining why a value is missing.

validation: allowed member values ;; delimiter declared ;; no duplicate members
short_desc: Zero or more levels per record.
detail: A multi-select delimited set. Member encoding (code/label) plus delim=<char>.

validation: order declared ;; allowed values ;; reverse-coded documented
short_desc: Ordered levels implying magnitude or interval.
detail: An ordinal scale where distance/direction carries meaning.
A symmetric agree-disagree response scale.
A bounded rating (stars, 1-10).

validation: unique ranks where required ;; bounded by option count
detail: An ordering of choices by preference.
School grade (K-12); ordered with roughly interval spacing.

validation: exactly two valid states ;; distinguish missing from false
detail: The reader-level boolean family. Format = preset encodings unioned with | plus a blank= policy.
A single two-valued flag. Case-insensitive, trimmed; blank= sets the missing policy.
A dummy variable marking presence of a condition.
A checkbox-style flag where blank means absent (false).
A two-state status via an explicit token set.
A binary survey answer; refusal/missing kept separate.
Whether a unit meets eligibility criteria.

validation: valid calendar/time value ;; declared parsing convention ;; range check
short_desc: A point or span in time.
detail: The reader-level temporal family. ISO-8601 is the canonical stable form for points.

validation: valid calendar date ;; no impossible dates
detail: A day-resolution date. Stabilized to ISO yyyymmdd; raw order/separator recorded in raw_data_format.

short_desc: A date plus time of day.
detail: A timestamp resolving to a moment.
A clock time with no calendar date.

validation: valid period ;; convention declared ;; period range
detail: A span longer than a day named as a unit. Grain selects the render graphic, so it stays operational.

validation: valid year range ;; fiscal/calendar convention declared
detail: A calendar or fiscal year.
A calendar or fiscal quarter.
A year-month period; drives the monthly calendar graphic.
An academic or fiscal semester.
A named season span.
A fiscal or reporting window with a start and end.

short_desc: A cyclical position within a cycle.
detail: A recurring position (hour within a day, weekday within a week).
Hour position 0-23.
Weekday position; drives the day-of-week graphic.
ISO or US week number.
Recurring month position (Jan-Dec), not tied to a year.
Recurring season position.

validation: start <= end ;; open/closed bounds declared ;; overlap rules
detail: A pair of time points bounding a span.
A start and end calendar date.

validation: preserve exact representation ;; no arithmetic ;; preserve leading zeros
short_desc: A label that names or keys an entity.
detail: The identifier family. Format = a named scheme (system:scheme) when one exists, else a COBOL-picture mask.

validation: unique where required ;; non-missing where required ;; stable across versions
detail: Any key or code. Mask for custom IDs; named scheme for registered ones.
A per-row primary key (serial, UUID, slug).

validation: unique within entity domain ;; stable over time
detail: Names a real-world entity (accession, ORG-001, gene/protein IDs).

validation: domain-specific pattern ;; checksum where available ;; preserve leading zeros
detail: A government or registry identifier with a pattern or checksum. Tier 1 (checksum): npi, orcid, isbn, issn, dea. Tier 2 (structure/prefix): ssn, ein, doi.

validation: fixed length ;; preserve leading zeros ;; valid vintage ;; hierarchy consistency
detail: A geographic code used as a key. Format defers to the geographic tokens; atomized components take a width suffix (fips:county3).
A content hash used as an identifier (MD5, SHA-256, UUID).

validation: valid version syntax ;; monotonicity where expected
detail: A version or revision tag (semver-style).

short_desc: A composite value holding multiple elements.
detail: The structured family: one cell containing a collection or record.

short_desc: An ordered/unordered set of elements (default structured class).
detail: A collection of like elements in one cell.
A variable-length collection.
A fixed-shape multi-dimensional collection.

short_desc: A keyed record (default structured class for objects).
detail: A composite of named fields in one cell.

validation: schema version ;; no unexpected keys where strict
detail: A schema-bearing record.

validation: unique keys ;; allowed keys ;; value-type rules
detail: A dictionary of key to value.

validation: valid geometry ;; CRS declared ;; coordinate bounds
detail: A geographic shape or packed coordinate pair. epsg:4326:latlon = lat-first pair; epsg:4326:lonlat = GeoJSON order.

validation: retain original values ;; do not coerce automatically ;; profile candidate types
detail: The fallback family: values whose type could not be resolved. Kept as text; never auto-coerced.
No confident type. Retain and profile.
Multiple value types share one column.

validation: retain source text ;; log parse errors ;; quantify failure rate
detail: Values that failed to parse; retained verbatim for review.
